item: Producer: choose a build platform able to reach the target Build level (L1+)
repo_note: Builds run on the CI host with federated credentials; no target level is chosen or recorded in an ADR.

item: Producer: build the same way every time so a verifier can form expectations (L1+)
repo_note: Fixed step order, generate once from the deployed revision, pinned inputs.

item: Producer: distribute provenance to consumers, or through the package ecosystem (L1+)
repo_note: No provenance to distribute; the deploy step and auditors are the consumers for a SaaS.

item: Platform: provenance exists, names the output by digest and says how it was built (L1+)
repo_note: Build identity and changelog tie a build to a run and a commit range; no provenance document (33 §4).

item: Platform: provenance is authentic, verifiable by consumers, normally signed (L2+)
repo_note: Nothing signs or verifies build output.

item: Platform: provenance is unforgeable; signing material out of reach of build steps (L3)
repo_note: Credentials are short-lived per run, but no signing key exists to isolate.

item: Platform: build steps run on a hosted platform, not a workstation (L2+)
repo_note: Deploys build in the pipeline; manual emergency applies allowed; macOS runner may also be a person's machine.

item: Platform: each build is isolated and ephemeral; no cache poisoning, no access to platform secrets (L3)
repo_note: Install scripts off and runner cleanup; self-hosted runners persist state; no ephemeral-runner or cache-isolation rule.

item: Org: choose a source control system able to reach the target Source level (L1+)
repo_note: A git host with branches is assumed; no target level chosen.

item: Org: configure the git host to control access and enforce history (L2+)
repo_note: No-rewrite rules are behaviour; nothing requires the host to enforce them.

item: Org: a documented, logged process for removing content from history, for legal or privacy reasons only (L2+)
repo_note: Leaked secrets are rotated, not expunged; no expunging process.

item: Org: evidence that each claimed technical control is continuously enforced (L3+)
repo_note: What gates a merge is written down; no evidence of enforcement over time.

item: Host: each repository has a stable unique identifier (L1+)
repo_note: Met by any git host.

item: Host: revisions are immutable and uniquely identified (L1+)
repo_note: Git commit ids; the set already relies on SHAs.

item: Host: reviewers see a human-readable form of each change (L1+)
repo_note: No generated files in the diff; contract-difference report; the plan is the review.

item: Host: issues verification summary attestations for revisions (L1+)
repo_note: No rule; depends on host or a separate tool.

item: Host: protected branches keep their full change history (L2+)
repo_note: Force-push banned for agents and people; host not required to refuse it.

item: Host: continuity of each control is tracked from a start revision (L2+)
repo_note: No record of when a control was turned on or lapsed.

item: Host: identifies and authenticates every actor (L2+)
repo_note: Pipeline identities federated; no MFA rule for human git-host accounts (33 §6.1 item 3).

item: Host: produces source provenance for each revision (L2+)
repo_note: No source provenance.

item: Host: named references are protected by technical controls (L3+)
repo_note: Production role trusts the release branch only; no host branch or tag protection rule.

item: Host: two different trusted persons agree to each change on a protected branch (L4)
repo_note: Review is required in places; no host-enforced second approver; agent plus owner is one identity.

item: No executables committed to the repository (private and open source)
repo_note: Build output never committed; binaries downloaded by hash instead.

item: Default and release branches protected: review, checks, no force-push or deletion (private and open source)
repo_note: Branch flow and gates written down; host settings not required; needs admin token to read.

item: Tests run on pull requests before merge (private and open source)
repo_note: Contract and supply-chain checks on every PR; unit and integration suites run on the branch, not the PR.

item: OpenSSF Best Practices badge (open source)
repo_note: Badge programme for open-source projects.

item: Changes reviewed by a human before merge (private and open source)
repo_note: Review named for plans, deps and ADRs; no rule that every merge has a second approver.

item: Recent contributors from several organisations (open source)
repo_note: Project-health signal; meaningless for a private team.

item: No untrusted checkout in privileged triggers, no script injection from event text (private and open source)
repo_note: Branch-scoped roles limit cloud reach; no rule on workflow triggers or event-text interpolation.

item: An automated dependency updater is on (private and open source)
repo_note: Weekly updater with 7-day cooldown, also updates action pins.

item: Fuzz or property-based tests (private and open source)
repo_note: Example-based and mutation-minded tests only.

item: A licence file is published (open source)
repo_note: A private product publishes no licence; third-party licence checks are a separate matter.

item: Recent commit and issue activity (open source)
repo_note: Signal for a consumer choosing a dependency; the product's consumers are its own team.

item: Published as a package through a packaging workflow (open source)
repo_note: Nothing is published to a package registry; app-store delivery is [32](../32-mobile-delivery.md).

item: Build and release inputs pinned by hash (private and open source)
repo_note: Actions by SHA, images by digest, requirements and downloads by hash, guard-tested.

item: Static analysis runs on changes (private and open source)
repo_note: No SAST rule.

item: A bill of materials in the source or the releases (private and open source)
repo_note: No SBOM rule.

item: A security policy naming how to report a vulnerability (private and open source, as security.txt for SaaS)
repo_note: No disclosure policy or security.txt.

item: Release artifacts are signed or carry provenance (private and open source)
repo_note: Mobile builds are signed for the stores; API and web bundles carry no signature or provenance.

item: Workflow token read-only by default, write granted per job (private and open source)
repo_note: Cloud credentials scoped; the CI host's own token permissions not addressed.

item: No open known vulnerabilities in the project or its dependencies (private and open source)
repo_note: New advisories blocked; existing ones listed with no fix deadline.

item: Repository webhooks authenticate with a secret (private and open source)
repo_note: Product verifies inbound webhooks; git-host webhooks not addressed; needs admin token to read.

item: Define security requirements for software development, keep them current, pass them to suppliers
repo_note: Requirements written and ASVS level recorded; none passed to commercial suppliers.

item: Implement roles and responsibilities, role-based training, management commitment
repo_note: Owner approvals named; training and management commitment are organisational.

item: Implement supporting toolchains and keep evidence of their use
repo_note: Checks named per event; no SAST or secret scanning; short artifact retention keeps little evidence.

item: Define and use criteria for software security checks
repo_note: Each check states when it fails; reviews need evidence per row.

item: Implement and maintain secure environments for development
repo_note: Separate accounts, no long-lived keys, install scripts off; developer endpoints and runner patching not covered.

item: Protect all forms of code from unauthorised access and tampering
repo_note: No secrets in code, no history rewrites; no host branch protection, commit signing or MFA rule.

item: Provide a way to verify the integrity of each release
repo_note: Mobile store signing only; no digest, signature or provenance for API and web releases.

item: Archive and protect each release and its provenance data
repo_note: Changelog, build identity and maps per release; no archived digest, provenance or SBOM.

item: Design software to meet security requirements and reduce risk
repo_note: Threat model per boundary and security questions per spec; no per-feature abuse cases.

item: Review the design against the security requirements and risks
repo_note: ADR reviewed with the code; no named security review of a design.

item: Reuse well-secured software, and check acquired components meet the requirements
repo_note: Named approval, registry checks, release age, advisories, prefer existing code.

item: Write code to secure coding practices
repo_note: Validation and parameterised queries; no rule on HTML sinks or outbound requests (33 §6.1).

item: Configure compilers, interpreters and build processes for executable security
repo_note: Strict typecheck, fail-closed generation, scripts off; no compiler or bundler hardening settings named.

item: Review or analyse human-readable code for vulnerabilities
repo_note: Review and pitfalls walk; no SAST and no security-focused review checklist.

item: Test executable code for vulnerabilities
repo_note: Pen-test plan and guard tests; no DAST or fuzzing.

item: Ship secure settings by default
repo_note: Free settings guard-tested; anonymous role and privacy flag explicit; generation fails closed.

item: Identify and confirm vulnerabilities on an ongoing basis
repo_note: Scheduled advisory job; no disclosure policy or intake for outside reports.

item: Assess, prioritise and fix vulnerabilities
repo_note: Every gap ends in an owner or ADR; no fix deadline for a known advisory (33 §6.1 item 6).

item: Analyse vulnerabilities to find their root causes
repo_note: A missed defect adds a rule and a pitfall; no search for other instances of the same flaw.
